_note: The class of lines a later slice writes when it stores a marker in the Kind byte of a store page (U-201's SubtreeUnfinished at 0x80), against the lines the store legitimately has in that column. SL-111 computes the subtree answer instead of storing it, so nothing in Store/** writes a marker today; this corpus holds that: KindByteWriteCorpusTests feeds every row to a closed grammar and runs the same grammar over every line of src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/**/*.cs. The grammar accepts a few forms of a line that names the Kind column and refuses the rest, so a spelling nobody listed (a compound assignment, an alias of the column, a ref to an element, a helper that returns the value) is refused too. The class is bounded by who writes such a line: a slice that adds a Kind-bit marker to ScanStore, by accident or on purpose. Rows listed under outside_the_bound are not caught and are pinned as 'miss' so a change to that is seen.

bounded_by.producers: A later slice that stores a flag in the Kind byte of Store/** by an ordinary spelling: a compound assignment, an assignment whose right side is not the whole Kind value, an alias or span of the column, a ref to an element, or a helper that returns the marked value.
bounded_by.member: One line in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/**/*.cs that names the Kind column of a page (Kind[...], or Kind with no index) other than by comparing an element with an EntryKind, switching on it, casting it to EntryKind, declaring the column, or the one whole write `Kind[i] = (byte)kind;`.
bounded_by.why_it_matters: ScanStore.Kind(), Charges, CheckParent, RolledSize, FilesBelow, ChildrenLargestFirst, OnDiskAtOrBelow and NotListedAtOrBelow (entry check and backward block scan) compare the raw Kind byte with EntryKind values. A bit OR-ed into the byte makes a marked folder read as a non-folder in all of them, so charges, rollups and child lists go silently wrong. A slice that stores the marker must mask every one of those reads first and then edit the grammar on purpose.

outside_the_bound.why: The grammar reads the text of Store/**/*.cs and nothing else. A value OR-ed into the kind before the one whole write (a marked EntryKind passed to Append, or `kind |= ...` on its own statement) leaves the write line as it is; a write from code outside Store/** is impossible while Page stays a private nested class of ScanStore; an identifier spelled with a unicode escape is not a spelling an ordinary producer reaches for.
